text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is often called the "silent killer" because most people do not have any warning signs or symptoms, even if their numbers are high.
snippet_highlighted_words: most people do not have any warning signs or symptoms

text_blocks.snippet: Symptoms rarely happen unless blood pressure rises to dangerous, life-threatening levels (such as a hypertensive crisis of 180/120 mm Hg or higher). In those cases, warning signs may include:

list.snippet: Blurred vision or other vision changes

text_blocks.snippet: What to Do in an Emergency
According to the American Heart Association, if your blood pressure reading is 180/120 mm Hg or higher:

list.snippet: Wait one minute and take the reading again.
If it remains that high and you have symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, weakness, vision changes, or difficulty speaking, call 911 immediately.
If your reading is 180/120 mm Hg or higher without those symptoms, contact your doctor right away for guidance.
